arxiv-2107-11380.title: Instability of the Body-Centered Cubic Lattice within the Sticky Hard Sphere and Lennard-Jones Model obtained from Exact Lattice Summations
arxiv-2107-11380.creator: Antony Burrows, Shaun Cooper, Peter Schwerdtfeger
arxiv-2107-11380.description: Abstract A smooth path of rearrangement from the body-centered cubic (bcc) to the face-centered cubic (fcc) lattice is obtained by introducing a single parameter to cuboidal lattice vectors. As a result, we obtain analytical expressions in terms of lattice sums for the cohesive energy.

arxiv-2306-14924.title: LLM-Assisted Content Analysis: Using Large Language Models to Support Deductive Coding
arxiv-2306-14924.creator: Robert Chew, John Bollenbacher, Michael Wenger, Jessica Speer, Annice Kim
arxiv-2306-14924.description: Abstract Deductive coding is a widely used qualitative research method for determining the prevalence of themes across documents. While useful, deductive coding is often burdensome and time consuming since it requires researchers to read, interpret, and reliably categorize a large body of unstructured text documents.

arxiv-2409-11527.title: Improving LLM Reasoning with Multi-Agent Tree-of-Thought Validator Agent
arxiv-2409-11527.creator: Fatemeh Haji, Mazal Bethany, Maryam Tabar, Cho-Yu Jason Chiang, Anthony Rios, Peyman Najafirad
arxiv-2409-11527.description: Abstract Multi-agent strategies have emerged as a promising approach to enhance the reasoning abilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) by assigning specialized roles in the problem-solving process. Concurrently, Tree of Thoughts (ToT) methods have shown potential in improving reasoning for complex question-answering tasks by exploring diverse reasoning paths.

arxiv-2505-05578.title: The survivorship bias of protoplanetary disc populations
arxiv-2505-05578.creator: Lorenzo A. Malanga, Giovanni P. Rosotti, Giuseppe Lodato, Alice Somigliana, Carlo F. Manara, Claudia Toci, Leonardo Testi
arxiv-2505-05578.description: Abstract The evolution of protoplanetary discs has a substantial impact on theories of planet formation. To date, neither of the two main competing evolutionary models, namely the viscous-photoevaporative paradigm and the MHD winds model, has been ruled out by observations.

arxiv-2505-15438.title: Bridging Sign and Spoken Languages: Pseudo Gloss Generation for Sign Language Translation
arxiv-2505-15438.creator: Jianyuan Guo, Peike Li, Trevor Cohn
arxiv-2505-15438.description: Abstract Sign Language Translation (SLT) aims to map sign language videos to spoken language text. A common approach relies on gloss annotations as an intermediate representation, decomposing SLT into two sub-tasks: video-to-gloss recognition and gloss-to-text translation. While effective, this paradigm depends on expert-annotated gloss labels, which are costly and rarely available in existing datasets, limiting its scalability.

arxiv-2508-19743.title: Superoptimal continued fractions
arxiv-2508-19743.creator: Slade Sanderson
arxiv-2508-19743.description: Abstract . Motivated by the optimal continued fractions studied independently by Selenius and Bosma, we define and introduce algorithms producing superoptimal continued fraction expansions of irrationals. These expansions simultaneously provide arbitrarily good rational approximations and converge arbitrarily quickly. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification 11K50 (Primary) 11J70; 37A44 (Secondary) 1.

arxiv-2510-15304.title: Layer as Puzzle Pieces: Compressing Large Language Models through Layer Concatenation
arxiv-2510-15304.creator: Fei Wang, Li Shen, Liang Ding, Chao Xue, Ye Liu, Changxing Ding
arxiv-2510-15304.description: Abstract Large Language Models excel at natural language processing tasks, but their massive size leads to high computational and storage demands. Recent works have sought to reduce their model size through layer-wise structured pruning. However, they tend to ignore retaining the capabilities in the pruned part.

arxiv-2510-18581.title: The Cost-Benefit of Interdisciplinarity in AI for Mental Health
arxiv-2510-18581.creator: \name Katerina Drakos \addr Center for Social Data Science, Faculty of Social Sciences, University of Copenhagen \email kda@sodas.ku.dk
arxiv-2510-18581.description: Abstract Artificial intelligence has been introduced as a way to improve access to mental health support. However, most AI mental health chatbots rely on a limited range of disciplinary input, and fail to integrate expertise across the chatbot’s lifecycle. This paper examines the cost-benefit trade-off of interdisciplinary collaboration in AI mental health chatbots.

pmc-10591561.title: O039 A Novel Approach to Quantify Breathing effort in Obstructive Sleep Apnoea
pmc-10591561.creator: P Nguyen, B Lechat, K Reynolds, D Eckert, P Catcheside
pmc-10591561.description: IntroductionBreathing effort is an important component of obstructed breathing and determinant of arousal in obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA). However, relative effects of hypopnoea versus apnoea on effort and work of breathing (WOB) are largely unknown. This study applied a novel modelling approach to quantify breathing effort, WOB and obstruction severity to evaluate differences between hypopnoea and apnoea events in OSA.

pmc-11453899.title: 6396 Recurrent hyperparathyroidism due to parathyromatosis
pmc-11453899.creator: A Valenciaga, M N Rayan, S W Ing
pmc-11453899.description: Disclosure: A. Valenciaga: None. M.N. Rayan: None. S.W. Ing: None. Background: Parathyromatosis is a rare cause of hyperparathyroidism. It refers to numerous parathyroid tissue foci within the neck and mediastinum, arising from the expansion of embryologic parathyroid tissue or due to the dissemination of parathyroid cells during surgical resection of abnormal parathyroid glands.

pmc-11475680.title: Bibliometric Analysis of Research on Exercise Intervention for Cancer-Related Cognitive Impairments
pmc-11475680.creator: Yuwei Shen, Ningsheng Xu, Tingting Yu, Jianan Li
pmc-11475680.description: Introduction: Cancer treatments frequently lead to cognitive impairments, affecting a substantial global population. Among various approaches, exercise has emerged as a promising strategy for rehabilitation. However, a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of research in this field is lacking. Methods: We conducted a bibliometric analysis of 10,345 articles sourced from the Web of Science database using the R package “bibliometrix”.

pmc-11487982.title: Research progress on the pathogenesis of multiple symmetrical lipomatosis
pmc-11487982.creator: Bo Hu, Ze Wang, Tengxiao Ma, Pengfei Fan, Lei Li
pmc-11487982.description: Multiple symmetric lipomatosis, also known as madelung’s disease, is a rare syndrome characterized by the accumulation of multiple symmetric subcutaneous adipose tissues that significantly affect patients’ quality of life. Since the aetiology of the disease is still unclear, surgical intervention by doctors based on clinical experience is currently the main treatment.

pmc-11611510.title: Associated Factors for Chronic Kidney Disease in Patients with Diabetes Mellitus 2: Retrospective Study
pmc-11611510.creator: Evelyn Del Socorro Goicochea-Rios, Irma Luz Yupari-Azabache, Nélida Milly Otiniano, Néstor Iván Gómez Goicochea
pmc-11611510.description: IntroductionChronic kidney disease affects the quality of life of people with diabetes mellitus, increases cardiovascular risk, and has high social costs.ObjectiveTo determine associated factors for chronic kidney disease in people with diabetes mellitus type 2.Material and MethodsRetrospective cohort study with 371 patients evaluated in primary care for diabetes mellitus.

pmc-12429772.title: Polynucleotides Enhance Collagen Synthesis via Modulating Phosphoenolpyruvate Carboxykinase 1 in Senescent Macrophages: Experimental Evidence
pmc-12429772.creator: Kyung-A Byun, Hyun Jun Park, Seyeon Oh, Kuk Hui Son, Kyunghee Byun, Mihaela Violeta Ghica
pmc-12429772.description: Polynucleotide (PN), a high-molecular-weight DNA fragment derived from salmon and other fish sources, shows promising anti-aging and regenerative effects on the skin. This study investigated how PN enhances collagen synthesis, focusing on its effect on phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase 1 (PCK1) in senescent macrophages and its downstream effects on fibroblasts.

pmc-12509676.title: Genome sequence of Mediterraneibacter faecis SZCH001, isolated from an autistic child
pmc-12509676.creator: Zhongsheng Zhu, Jiaojie Guan, Xiuxiu Xie, Chuqing Zhang, Zili Liao, Ziyuan Li, Boxian Lin, Hu Chen, Zeling Zhuang, Shiyun Meng, Yigui Zou, Wenwen Li, Mingjing Luo, Dongling Dai
pmc-12509676.description: Here, we report the draft genome sequence of Mediterraneibacter faecis SZCH001, isolated from a fecal sample of an autistic child. The bacterial genome was sequenced using Illumina technology on a Novaseq 6000 platform. The assembled genome of M. faecis comprises 3,423,666 base pairs with a G+C content of 40.27%.

pmc-12629529.title: Three-Month cART Initiated During Primary HIV Does Not Correct the Structural, Immune, and Microbial Abnormalities within the Gastrointestinal Tract
pmc-12629529.creator: Camilla Tincati, Valeria Bono, Silvia Nozza, Alessandra Bandera, Delfina Tosi, Valentina Sala, Giuseppe Ancona, Andrea Calcagno, Antonio Muscatello, Stefano Rusconi, Matteo Augello, Roberta Rovito, Umberto Gianelli, Carlo Pescia, Andrea Santoro, Monica Falleni, Andrea Gori, Giulia Marchetti
pmc-12629529.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background:HIV infection leads to profound alterations of gut structure, immunity, and microbiome, resulting in immune activation and inflammation, which drive the development of non-infectious comorbidities. The introduction of combination antiretroviral therapy (cART) in the chronic stages of disease does not correct such abnormalities; however, the effect of viro-suppressive treatment in the gastrointestinal tract during primary HIV infection (PHI) is largely unknown.

pmc-12649408.title: Anticandidal Activity and Low Cytotoxicity of Modified Analogues of the Tobacco Defensin NaD1
pmc-12649408.creator: Olga V Shevchenko, Ivan V Bogdanov, Serafima I Fateeva, Daria N Melnikova, Anastasia A Ignatova, Ilia Y Toropygin, Tatiana V Ovchinnikova, Ekaterina I Finkina, Fernando Albericio
pmc-12649408.description: Background/Objectives: The growing resistance development among fungi, including those of Candida species, poses significant challenges to public health, emphasizing the need for the implementation of innovative therapeutic approaches. The tobacco defensin NaD1 exhibits a pronounced activity against C. albicans, but its relatively high cytotoxicity toward mammalian cells limits its potential application.

pmc-12702073.title: A Gly-β-muricholic acid and FGF15 combination therapy synergistically reduces “humanized” bile acid pool toxicity in cholestasis mice
pmc-12702073.creator: Mohammad Nazmul Hasan, Huaiwen Wang, Wenyi Luo, Yanhong Du, Lei Xiong, Lijie Gu, Tiangang Li
pmc-12702073.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Hydrophobic bile acid-mediated hepatobiliary injury is a major driver of cholestasis progression. Most anticholestasis treatments being tested clinically are based on a single agent, which does not always sufficiently alleviate bile acid toxicity to slow disease progression. This study investigates a therapeutic strategy of combining glycine-conjugated β-muricholic acid (Gly-βMCA) and fibroblast growth factor-15 (FGF15) to alleviate bile acid hepatobiliary toxicity in Cyp2c70 KO mice that lack endogenous muricholic acid (MCA) synthesis and have a “humanized” hydrophobic bile acid pool composition.

pmc-12874367.title: Computational Workflow to Unravel the Structural Dynamics of Supramolecular Metallacages in Solution
pmc-12874367.creator: Julia A. Stebani, Iñigo Iribarren Aguirre, Gohar A. Siddiqui, Darren Wragg, Alessio Gagliardi, Angela Casini
pmc-12874367.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The structural dynamics of self-assembled metallacages is important because it determines their function and stability in different applications involving encapsulation and release of a guest molecule. We present here an integrated computational workflow to study the dynamic behavior of selected [Pd2L4]4+ metallacages in explicit solvents (water and DMSO) and benchmark them for future in silico investigations of their host–guest chemistry, pivotal to their application as drug delivery systems.

pmc-12976155.title: Preferences and Perceptions of Training Models in Global Surgery With a Focus on Orthopedics: A Scoping Review
pmc-12976155.creator: Harlene Kaur, Daniel Flynn, Andrew Haggarty, Sanjeev Sabharwal
pmc-12976155.description: Purpose of ReviewThis scoping review examines learner-reported preferences and experiences with remote learning, observership, and visiting-surgeon exchange models in low-resource settings. We outline potential benefits, limitations, equity considerations, and evidence gaps that can inform ethical and sustainable global orthopaedic education partnerships.

pmc-13267162.title: Distant Presence: Care Workers' Experiences of Digital Monitoring Systems in Dementia Care
pmc-13267162.creator: Clara Iversen, David Redmalm, Marcus Persson, Elin Thunman
pmc-13267162.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Aims and ObjectivesTo add nuance to when and how remote technologies should be used to support dementia care, we examine care workers' experiences of two phone‐based digital systems used for monitoring and planning in daily care.Methodological Design and JustificationShort‐term ethnography at three care homes, 49 qualitative interviews, and five video‐recorded situations provided data for a detailed account of care workers' experiences of the digital systems.

pmc-13358255.title: Transanal irrigation for the management of low anterior resection syndrome (LARS): protocol for a pragmatic, multicentre, crossover randomised controlled trial
pmc-13358255.creator: Jessica Holland, Marie Demian, Sarah Sabboobeh, Camila L P Oliveira, Li Tang, Sahir Bhatnagar, A Sender Liberman, Sébastien Drolet, Carl Brown, Caitlin Cahill, Sepehr Khorasani, Terry Zwiep, Carol-Ann Vasilevsky, Nancy Morin, Allison Pang, Richard Garfinkle, Sami A Chadi, Shafic Abdulkarim, Gordon B
pmc-13358255.description: IntroductionAdvances in surgical techniques and neoadjuvant care for rectal cancer have increased sphincter preservation, allowing restoration of bowel continuity through low anterior resection (LAR). However, up to 75% of patients experience low anterior resection syndrome (LARS), which is bowel dysfunction characterised by faecal incontinence, frequency, urgency and clustering of bowel movements, significantly impairing quality of life (QoL).

pmc-13438818.title: Enhancing nursing students’ moral sensitivity through the World Cafe and ethical decision-making simulation to address diverse learning styles
pmc-13438818.creator: Hsiao Lu Lee, Chiu-Yueh Hsiao
pmc-13438818.description: Teachers’ instructional strategies and students’ learning styles are key determinants of learning effectiveness. This study examined whether the World Cafe teaching strategy and the Four-Topic Approach to ethical decision-making could enhance outcomes in nursing ethics education. A total of 250 nursing students participated in this study.

pmc-13564706.title: Physical and Biochemical Determinants of Endocrine Fate in 3D Suspension Culture Based Stem Cell-Derived β-Cell Differentiation
pmc-13564706.creator: Roberto Castro-Gutierrez, Ali H. Shilleh, Jessie M. Barra, Shane P. M. Williams, Balachandar Nedumaran, Taylor M. Triolo, Matthias Hebrok, Holger A. Russ
pmc-13564706.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Efficient and reproducible generation of functional stem cell-derived β cells (sBC) remains a major challenge for basic research and cell replacement therapy, partly due to incomplete understanding of endocrine induction during differentiation and challenges with clinical scale-up. Here, we dissect the individual contributions of commonly used endocrine differentiation factors on pancreatic progenitor maintenance, endocrine commitment, and hormone subset generation in a scalable 3D differentiation system. We demonstrated that starting pluripotent stem cell cluster size is a critical determinant for downstream sBC generation.

pmc-13604198.title: Exercise Modulates Working Memory-Related Brain Activation Through Bidirectional Neural Mechanisms: An ALE Meta-Analysis of Longitudinal and Cross-Sectional fMRI Studies
pmc-13604198.creator: Jiayu Wang, Jun Wang, Wenshuang Tang
pmc-13604198.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background: Physical exercise improves working memory (WM) across the lifespan, yet the neural mechanisms underlying this benefit remain incompletely understood, and it is unclear whether intervention-induced neuroplastic changes and long-term exercise-related differences converge on common neural circuits. Methods: We systematically searched PubMed, Web of Science, PsycINFO, and CNKI through June 2026 and included 11 task-based fMRI studies (6 longitudinal interventions and 5 cross-sectional comparisons; 403 participants) reporting whole-brain activation coordinates.
